title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Agentic Manipulation Policies (AMP1)

### The Breakthrough
AMP1 uses a generalist AI model as the sole robot controller, achieving zero‑shot success on the RoboLab‑120 benchmark (85.6% versus 49.2% for the next best) and winning 104 of 108 real‑world trials across twelve tasks, demonstrating on‑the‑fly grasping, pushing and tool use without task‑specific training.

### The Caveats
The claim of broad robustness is limited to RoboLab‑120, CaP‑Gym and RoboDojo suites; no other environments were tested.

## ASTRA Space Assembly

### The Breakthrough
ASTRA combines a six‑DOF arm with motorized dispensers to autonomously pick, position and join truss struts and a reflective Kapton‑based net in low‑Earth orbit, completing the first fully autonomous structural build in space and confirming the result with downlinked photos.

### The Caveats
Scalability rests on a single‑bay demo with no comparative metrics, leaving larger‑structure feasibility unproven.

## COBRA Snake Robot Whole‑Body Loco‑Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
A contact‑implicit dynamics model based on the Moreau‑Jean scheme feeds a full‑order trajectory optimizer, letting a hyper‑redundant snake robot push objects while sidewinding; hardware experiments validate the approach across multiple configurations.

### The Caveats
No quantitative comparison to existing loco‑manipulation methods is provided.

## Agentic Robotics Coding Agents

### The Breakthrough
LLM‑driven coding agents automatically generate and refine robot control code in high‑fidelity simulation, reaching 99% success on simulated tasks and matching hand‑engineered pipelines without any human‑collected data.

### The Caveats
All results are confined to simulation; real‑world robot tests are absent.

## Agentic Robotics Graph‑as‑Policy (Berkeley/NVIDIA)

### The Breakthrough
The Graph‑as‑Policy framework decomposes tasks into modular skills that AI agents rehearse in NVIDIA Isaac simulation, yielding a 15,000‑package‑per‑robot throughput boost in a warehouse demo and successful transfer to a physical robot, with open‑source code and a new benchmark released.

### The Caveats
The reported throughput gain lacks a baseline comparison, so its magnitude is unverified.

## Grasp‑TAGS Task‑Aware Grasp Selection

### The Breakthrough
By distilling a PPO critic into a fast grasp‑utility network, Grasp‑TAGS selects task‑optimal grasps, improving rearrangement success to 89.84% (≈10 pts over the best single‑grasp baseline) and reducing final orientation error.

### The Caveats
The improvement is demonstrated only in simulation, with no hardware validation.

## Constrained Moving Horizon Estimator for Continuum Robots

### The Breakthrough
A constrained MHE incorporating non‑penetration constraints achieves 0.9 mm position error and 0.22 N force error in simulation, far outperforming a tuned EKF and remaining robust to obstacle pose and friction variations.

### The Caveats
Performance is shown solely in simulation; real‑robot tests are missing.

## Bionic Humanoid News Anchors

### The Breakthrough
UBTECH’s bionic‑skin humanoids equipped with an emotional large‑model AI read live news, pull verified content from Xinhua’s pipeline in real time, and support multilingual interaction while staying under editorial control.

### The Caveats
Only a single stage demo is presented, with no baseline or broader testing to substantiate the “first functional bionic news anchor” claim.

## OpenHarness Multi‑Agent Coding Harness

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness runs multiple LLM coding agents side‑by‑side in tmux panes, streams encrypted WebRTC text with sub‑15 ms latency and ~0.1 % CPU on an M2 Max, enabling a single CLI to launch and control agents across machines.

### The Caveats
No benchmarks compare it to existing multi‑agent IDEs or orchestration frameworks.

## Continuum Local‑First AI Citizens

### The Breakthrough
Continuum provides a Rust‑based platform where persistent agents run on‑device llama.cpp models, evolve via LoRA‑based genomes, and continuously learn from experience, with an integrated benchmark suite reporting scores.

### The Caveats
Benchmark scores lack baseline comparisons, leaving the claimed advantage unsubstantiated.

### Priority
AMP1’s real‑world, zero‑shot manipulation across diverse tasks shows a decisive step toward generalist embodied AI, making it the most consequential story today.

### One action
Visit the AMP1 repository on GitHub, clone the zero‑shot demo, and run it on your own robot to evaluate the generalist controller.

### What to watch
The three agentic‑robotics works (AMP1, LLM coding agents, and the Graph‑as‑Policy system) illustrate a rapid shift from simulation‑only code generation toward real‑world deployment of generalist AI controllers. Watch for upcoming real‑robot validations of the coding‑agent approach and quantitative benchmarks for the Graph‑as‑Policy throughput claims.
